meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'тоять'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to stand', forming an aspectual pair with 'постоять'.

examples.trans: Mom, why are you standing there? Come in.
I'm standing here.

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?

заходить.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to drop in
meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (root 'ходить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to come in', forming an aspectual pair with 'зайти'.

examples.trans: Mom, why are you standing there? Come in.
Please come in.
Come in, Fedya. Sit down on the chair.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (root 'ехать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to arrive', forming an aspectual pair with 'приезжать'.

examples.trans: Mom has arrived.
Which car did you come in?
Pasha has arrived.

meanings.note: Everyday conversational Russian interj meaning 'hi', frequent in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dima, hi. What are you doing?

пожить.gloss: to live for a while, to stay

meanings.en: to live for a while, to stay
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (root 'жить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to live for a while', forming an aspectual pair with 'жить'.

examples.trans: Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (root 'слышать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to hear', forming an aspectual pair with 'слышать'.

examples.trans: Mom will hear us.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (root 'пать'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to sleep', forming an aspectual pair with 'поспать'.

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.en: for a long time; long ago
meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'for a long time'.
